events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: The radio clicks on. Tuesday, February 2. Your clean shirt is folded exactly as the hotel left it. Record a voice memo nobody else can hear. It can be for Jo, for tomorrow's you, or for nobody at all. The small bottle of maple syrup is back on the dresser, wrapped and unopened. Choose what you physically do with it. The recorder is running. Before this Tuesday you remember 25 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.

choices.pack: Phil tucks the unopened maple syrup into his travel bag.
choices.leave: Phil leaves the wrapped bottle on the hotel dresser.
choices.open: Phil opens the bottle for himself this morning.
choices.pour_out: Phil empties the bottle into the hotel sink.

events.line: It stays on the dresser, Jo. Eight o'clock, sharp, and stop holding the line like you're waiting for a miracle.
events.effect: Phil leaves the wrapped bottle on the hotel dresser.

events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: Rita and Larry wait at the cue sheet. Beside it is the only weather cartridge: your own cheerful voice doing an old forecast, down to a small breath before your first word. At seven, it can substitute for you on air. Do something with it while they can see. They can hear anything you say. Before this Tuesday you remember 25 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.

choices.pocket_cart: Phil pockets the station's only copy of his old weather recording.
choices.mark_archive: Phil writes ARCHIVE across the weather cartridge and leaves it by the cue sheet.
choices.leave_cart: Phil leaves the weather cartridge by the cue sheet, unmarked.

events.line: Don't touch that, it's not a prop. You're on air with a ghost at seven.
events.effect: Phil writes ARCHIVE across the weather cartridge and leaves it by the cue sheet.

events.speaker: Rita
events.cue: You just saw Phil at the cue sheet. Speak to him or to Larry, or let the moment go.

choices.tear_carbon: Rita gives Phil the yellow carbon copy of the cue sheet.
choices.keep_carbon: Rita clips the yellow carbon back under her sheet.

events.line: Don't tell me what I'm on air with, Phil. You're not the one signing the check.
events.effect: Rita clips the yellow carbon back under her sheet.

events.speaker: Larry
events.cue: You're beside Rita. Phil can hear you. You can answer either one. The crew still has to get the equipment across the street.

choices.take_case: Larry picks up the equipment case.
choices.set_down: Larry sets the equipment case on the floor.

events.effect: Larry picks up the equipment case.

events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: The coach door is open. The projection booth across the street has a service door. There is a stairwell at the hotel where the radio can't be heard. Go where you actually want to go. You can speak under your breath. Before this Tuesday you remember 25 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.
events.line: Jo, the door is open, and the air in here tastes like copper. Eight o'clock, or I'm walking away from that couch.

events.speaker: Alma
events.cue: The door is shut. Only Rita and Larry are with you. You have the key; the last reel has eight minutes left. They can bring a microphone, give you one private line to Nell, or pack up. You have not given permission. Open the conversation however you like.

events.speaker: Larry
events.cue: Speak to Alma or Rita. They were not both at the hotel desk. You decide what to repeat, if anything. You have a pencil and an empty reel box.

choices.write_label: Larry turns the reel box over and writes on its blank label.

events.line: Don't breathe. She's just a voice on a dead channel, Alma.

events.speaker: Rita
events.cue: Alma and Larry are here with you. Their words are still in the room. There is exactly one line at seven. Ask for something you actually need, or refuse what's being asked.

choices.draw_chair: Rita pulls a chair over to Alma.
choices.stay_door: Rita stays by the closed door.

events.line: Larry, put the pencil down. I'm not letting a ghost fill this slot.
events.effect: Rita pulls a chair over to Alma.

events.speaker: Alma
events.cue: Answer the people here. You can reserve your voice for Nell, let people hear it publicly as well, or withhold it altogether. Their jobs do not oblige you to help.

choices.family_only: Alma permits only a private call to Nell.
choices.public_too: Alma permits either the public microphone or a private call.

events.line: Eight minutes is enough. Leave it running.

events.speaker: Larry
events.cue: One last thing you could say to either of them before the reel runs out.

choices.hold_door: Larry holds the door for Alma.

events.line: She's a voice on a dead channel, not a person. Don't breathe.

events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: There is a telephone here. You can ring Jo in Pittsburgh, or let her have the afternoon to herself. If you call, say what she hears when she picks up. If you leave it alone, keep the line empty. Before this Tuesday you remember 25 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.
events.line: Jo, it's me. I'm on the line, so stop looking under the cushions and just listen to my breathing for a second.

events.speaker: Jo
events.cue: Phil is on the telephone. You don't see his surroundings. One couch foot is still stuck. Answer him as you please.

choices.stay: Jo stays on the line for another beat.

events.line: I'm not under the cushions, I'm holding a button. And stop doing that voice. We need to lift the second leg off.
events.effect: Jo stays on the line for another beat.

events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: A town phone directory gives the regional station's desk number. You can call Rita there, tape something for yourself or stay quiet. If you call, she picks up; your line is the only part heard at the other end. Before this Tuesday you remember 25 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.

choices.call_desk: Rita picks up the station telephone.
choices.memo: Phil keeps this recording to himself.

events.line: Eight o'clock, sharp. Don't burn the pancakes.

events.speaker: Rita
events.cue: The phone is back on its cradle. Larry needs to know what to set up. Tell him what you want, or let him choose. He can still refuse.

choices.clear_space: Rita clears a space beside the patch.
choices.leave_space: Rita keeps her hands in her pockets.

events.line: You pick the reel. I'm out. Don't make it about me.
events.effect: Rita keeps her hands in her pockets.

events.speaker: Larry
events.cue: You have time to prepare one input. Answer the people in this room. The old recording is usable only if it is here.

choices.load_cart: Larry threads the old weather cartridge.
choices.set_mic: Larry tests the live microphone for Alma.

events.line: Don't make it about me, and don't make it about a ghost. It's eighteen-fifty-five. I'm not signing off on a dead channel again.

events.speaker: Rita
events.cue: Seven o'clock. Make the patch or let the slot go. Anything you say is to Larry and Alma inside the control room.

choices.silence: Rita lets the seven o’clock slot pass in silence.

events.effect: Rita lets the seven o’clock slot pass in silence.

events.speaker: Alma
events.cue: The slot is gone. Say what you want Rita and Larry to hear before you take your coat.

events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: At seven you tuned to the regional frequency. What you heard: The regional frequency carries room tone. You cannot tell why. Now, hours later, the pocket recorder clicks on in your hand. Leave a private voice memo for morning about the part of today you can still hear. Speak as Phil, or play out the silence. Before this Tuesday you remember 25 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.

choices.keep: Phil lets the last recording play to the end.

events.line: Just that hum. Don't let the static take it. Eight o'clock, sharp, and the syrup is in the bag.
events.effect: Phil lets the last recording play to the end.
